market_question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO before 2027?
reasoning: Ukraine’s constitution (2019) enshrines NATO membership as a strategic goal, and President Zelenskyy has repeatedly reaffirmed this aspiration. Publicly agreeing not to join—even temporarily—would be politically explosive and face immense domestic opposition. While a peace deal could force such a concession, the current trajectory and lack of serious negotiations make a formal pledge before 2027 highly unlikely.
evidence_points: Ukraine’s 2019 constitutional amendment commits the country to pursue NATO and EU membership.
Zelenskyy has consistently called for accelerated NATO accession, most recently at the 2024 NATO summit.
Any agreement would require a dramatic reversal by Ukraine, with no current indication of willingness.
Peace talks remain stalled, and Ukraine’s Western backers have not pressured it to abandon NATO ambitions.
Even a temporary suspension (e.g., 10 years) would be interpreted as a major strategic defeat, reducing its likelihood.
sources_consulted: Brookings Institution analysis on Ukraine-Russia peace scenarios
Recent NATO summit declarations regarding Ukraine
OSINT reports on Ukrainian public opinion regarding NATO
